newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS REVAMP CONTINUES WITH CABLE TV SALE.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS REVAMP CONTINUES WITH CABLE TV SALE.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV on Tuesday sent another message to financial markets that it was serious about tackling non-core units, announcing the planned sale of its cable television interests.

The Dutch electronics giant, which recently reported its first annual net loss since 1992, said it had signed a letter of intent to sell its 50 percent stake in cable television operator United and Philips Communications BV (UPC) to joint venture partner, United International Holdings Inc. of Denver, Colorado.
Philips said it would raise gross proceeds of about 800 million guilders ($424.6 million) through the transaction.
As part of the deal UPC will purchase all of Philips' 3.17 million shares of UIH class A common stock, a statement said.

A Philips spokesman said the deal was expected to be completed in the third quarter but declined to say how Philips planned to use the money raised by the sale, the latest in a string of disposals since last October when new chairman Cor Boonstra vowed to tackle underperforming Philips "bleeders".

"As is widely known, Philips is currently reviewing its portfolio of activities. As a result, the company has concluded that its cable TV operation is not a core activity," said President and CEO of Philips Media Richard de Lange.

"We said a few months ago that selling our stake in UPC would be an option," said Philips spokesman Ben Geerts, declining to say how much further the company had to go in ridding itself of non-core or underperforming businesses targeted by Boonstra.

Philips has embarked on a stringent restructuring plan to weed out non-core businesses and tighten management as a way of boosting profits, winding up or selling off units such as its Videoland and Superclub home entertainment businesses.

Another "bleeder", heavy loss-making German consumer electronics unit Grundig was pushed out to arm's length in January when Philips said it would no longer pick up the tab for 100 percent of its losses, instead consolidating the firm pro-rata to its 32 percent minority shareholding.
Analysts welcomed the UPC move as emphasising that Boonstra meant business in sorting out the company's weak spots and putting Philips back on track towards profit.

"There's more (restructuring) to come but maybe not as much as we've seen in the last three or four months," said Joost van Beek of Van Meer James Capel. "The largest of the bleeders have been attacked," he said.
Other analysts said the 800 million guilder gross proceeds for the deal compared well with the 482 million guilder book value for UPC in the 1996 annual report.
"At first glance it seems a fair price," said analyst Peter Wortel of Delta Lloyd Bank, adding it would help offset further restructuring costs he anticipated in 1997.
Van Beek, however, questioned the price, which equates by some methods of calculation to 800 guilders per connection, compared to the 1,400 guilders Philips has in the past paid.
"Two years ago everyone was chasing these networks and that drove up the price to around 1,400-1,500 guilders per subscriber," he said.

"On the basis of a 482 million guilder book value it looks like a good deal, but you have to take into account that some of the cable networks have been on the books for a long time and are booked at quite a low value," said Van Beek.

But he said the steps taken by Philips over recent months should help it towards its previously stated goal of postive cash flow of one billion guilders in 1997, clawing its way back from the 1996 negative cash flow of 1.86 billion guilders
Philips said 308 million guilders of the money to be raised via the planned UPC deal would be in the form of new securities, issued by UPC.
Philips will be able to sell these securities in the secondary market once the deal is completed.

UPC is Europe's largest private cable operator. On a proportionate basis, representing UPC's equity interest in various projects, it passes 1.9 million homes and has over 1.3 million subscribers, Philips said.

"This transaction enables us to fully capitalise on multi-channel television and other communication assets we have systematically put in place in 14 countries throughout Europe and in Israel," UIH chairman Gene Schneider said.
Philips shares were 1.30 guilders higher at 83.40 guilders in a strongly higher Amsterdam stock market.
